title: Vision LLMs and Content Understanding for parsing
summary: A vision model reads a page image directly and can explain charts and messy layouts that OCR flattens. Azure Content Understanding wraps analysis in schema-defined fields with confidence and grounding.
useIf: Pages carry meaning in charts, diagrams or irregular layouts, or you need typed fields with confidence and grounding rather than free text.
avoidIf: Documents are clean text or ordinary tables and you need cheap, repeatable output: layout analysis wins on cost and determinism.

explain.md: A **vision LLM** takes a page image and a prompt and returns text, Markdown or JSON. It can describe a chart, read a stamp or follow an odd layout that OCR turns into noise. The costs are real: image and output tokens per page, latency, and output that can differ between runs. Those costs and the determinism point below are engineering practice, not vendor figures: measure them on your pages.

**Azure Content Understanding** analyses documents, images, audio and video into schema-defined fields with confidence scores and grounding. API `2025-11-01` is GA and recommended for production. `2026-06-01-preview` adds signature detection, document metadata extraction and richer classification with in-page segmentation [[tr18]].

Inside Azure AI Search, the Content Understanding skill is GA in REST `2026-04-01`. It extracts and chunks in one skill, can let chunks span pages, and its `chunkingProperties` set `method` (`fixedSize` by default, `semantic` in preview since `2026-05-01-preview`), `unit` (`characters`, or `tokens` with `semantic` only), `maximumLength` (300 to 50,000 characters or 100 to 8,000 tokens, default 500) and `overlapLength` (below half of `maximumLength`, `fixedSize` only). AI image descriptions are preview and need an Azure OpenAI chat model on the attached Foundry resource [[tr19]]. Asynchronous documents are limited to 200 MB and 300 pages [[tr35]].

**Determinism matters for ingestion.** If a vision parse changes a few words on every run, your content hash changes, unchanged files look new and you re-embed them. Cache the parse keyed by file hash, parser version and prompt version, and re-parse only on purpose. Benchmarks such as OmniDocBench compare pipeline tools with end-to-end vision-language models, and ColPali skips parsing by embedding page images as multi-vector embeddings [[tr22]] [[tr39]].

whereToUse: Slide decks, dashboards and infographics where charts carry the facts
Invoices, forms and statements where typed fields with confidence feed a downstream system
Handwritten or irregular pages where classic OCR output is unusable
Figure captioning at ingest so charts become searchable text
Mixed media (documents, audio, video) analysed under one schema with Content Understanding

use: Use a vision model when the answer lives in a chart, diagram or irregular layout
Use Content Understanding when you need schema-defined fields, confidence scores and grounding
Use the Content Understanding skill when you want extraction and chunking in one indexing step
Use caching and validation for every model-based parser
avoid: Avoid a vision model as the default for plain text files: cost and variability buy nothing
Avoid trusting transcribed numbers without a cross-check against a second source
Avoid semantic chunking and image descriptions in production until their preview status changes
flips: Pages are mostly visual and retrieval of whole pages is enough: embed page images instead of parsing
Output must be reproducible for audit: prefer a layout model or cache every parse with versions
Volume is huge and layouts are uniform: a template-based layout model is cheaper than a vision call per page

pitfalls.symptom: Unchanged files are re-embedded on every run
pitfalls.cause: A vision parse returns slightly different text each time, so the content hash changes
pitfalls.fix: Cache parse output by file hash plus parser and prompt version, and hash the cached text

pitfalls.symptom: A table total is wrong in the answer
pitfalls.cause: The vision model transcribed a number incorrectly and nothing checked it
pitfalls.fix: Cross-check numbers against layout text and route mismatches to review

pitfalls.symptom: Pipeline breaks when semantic chunking is enabled
pitfalls.cause: Semantic chunking is preview in `2026-05-01-preview` and the GA API does not offer it
pitfalls.fix: Use `fixedSize` on `2026-04-01` and evaluate semantic chunking separately

pitfalls.symptom: Tables arrive as plain text from one skill and as Markdown from another
pitfalls.cause: The Content Understanding skill page and the Document Layout skill page disagree on table output
pitfalls.fix: Test both skills on your own tables before choosing

scenarios.title: Quarterly decks full of charts
scenarios.situation: An assistant answers questions about slide decks. Many answers sit in charts and diagrams. About 2,000 decks arrive per quarter and answers need not be byte-identical between runs.
constraints: Budget for a second pass on figures
unknowns: Do users ask for exact chart values or trends?
Can a human sample the output?
scenarios.question: How do you parse the decks?

options.name: Layout text for the slides, plus vision-generated captions for figures, cached and cross-checked
options.why: Text stays cheap and repeatable while charts become searchable sentences.
options.tradeoff: Two passes and a cache to maintain.

options.name: Vision model on every page
options.why: One uniform path that sees everything.
options.tradeoff: Highest token cost and the most run-to-run variation.

options.name: OCR text only
options.why: Chart content never becomes text, so those questions fail.

flips.then: Extract the underlying data when available and validate captions against it.

scenarios.takeaway: Spend vision tokens only on the regions where text parsing cannot see.

scenarios.title: Invoices feeding a finance system
scenarios.situation: Scanned supplier invoices must yield supplier, total and due date for a downstream system. Auditors want to see how confident each extraction is and where on the page it came from.
unknowns: What error rate is acceptable before human review?
scenarios.question: What do you use?

options.name: Content Understanding analyzer with a field schema, GA API `2025-11-01`
options.why: It returns schema-defined fields with confidence scores and grounding, which matches the audit need.
options.tradeoff: You design and test the schema and pay per analysis.

options.name: Vision LLM with a JSON schema and your own validation
options.tradeoff: You must build confidence, grounding and caching yourself.

options.name: OCR text plus regular expressions
options.tradeoff: Right for a single fixed template.

flips.if: A rare field needs the preview `2026-06-01-preview` features
flips.then: Isolate that path and label it preview.

flips.if: One uniform template covers 99 percent of invoices
flips.then: A cheaper template-based layout model suffices.

scenarios.takeaway: Typed fields with provenance favour an analyzer over a free-form prompt.

quiz.q: Which Content Understanding API version is GA and recommended for production as of 2026-10-13?
quiz.explain: `2025-11-01` is the GA version. `2026-06-01-preview` is a preview that adds signature detection and metadata extraction. `2024-11-30` is Document Intelligence v4.0 and `2026-08-01-preview` is an AI Search preview.

quiz.q: Which are genuine drawbacks of a general vision LLM as your page parser?
options: Image and output tokens add cost per page
quiz.explain: Variation, per-page token cost and transcription errors are the trade-offs. Reading charts is the strength, not a drawback.

quiz.q: Put the validation steps for vision parsing in order.
items: Parse the page with a fixed prompt and schema
Reject output that fails the schema
Cache with file hash and versions
quiz.explain: Cheap automatic checks come before human review, and the cache stores only output that survived them.

flashcards.front: Why can vision-based parsing cause re-embedding churn?
flashcards.back: Small run-to-run text differences change the content hash. Cache parses by file hash, parser version and prompt version.

flashcards.front: What does Content Understanding add over a plain prompt?
flashcards.back: Schema-defined fields with confidence scores and grounding across documents, images, audio and video.
